title: 题都城南庄
titleEn: Written at a Farmhouse South of the Capital
author: 崔护
intro: Last year a face and peach blossoms glowed pink together at this gate. This year the blossoms are back, still smiling in the spring wind — but the face is gone.
analysis: 这首诗只有四句，讲了一个故事。去年的今天，诗人在长安城南的一户人家门口，看见一位姑娘，她的脸和桃花互相映照，都是红红的。今年同一天他又来了，桃花还像去年一样在春风里开得灿烂，可是那位姑娘已经不知去了哪里。诗里用了对比：去年和今年，人和花，有和无。“人面”和“桃花”出现了两次，第一次在一起，第二次分开了。桃花“笑”春风，用的是拟人（把花当作人来写），花越开心，人越失落。后来“人面桃花”成了成语，比喻见过面、后来又见不到的心上人。
analysisEn: Four lines, one whole story. On this day last year, at a farmhouse gate south of Chang’an, the poet saw a young woman: her face and the peach blossoms lit each other up, both glowing pink. Exactly a year later he comes back. The peach blossoms are as bright as ever, smiling in the spring breeze — but the woman is gone, and he has no idea where. The poem is built on contrasts: last year and this year, the face and the flowers, there and not there. “Face” and “peach blossom” each appear twice — together the first time, apart the second. Describing the flowers as “smiling” treats them like people, and the happier they look, the emptier he feels. A later story fills in a romantic ending, but the poem itself stops at the empty gate, and that is its power. 人面桃花 became an idiom for someone you once met and lost, and the sense of returning to a place to find the person gone.
background: Cui Hu was a Tang poet who passed the highest examination in 796; little else is known about him. Tradition, recorded in a late-Tang story collection, says he wrote this on the farmhouse gate on his second visit.
pronunciation: 都城 dū（首都）。相映 xiāng。
version: 采用通行版本。第三句一作“人面只今何处在”，教材及通行本作“人面不知何处去”。

lines.py: qù nián jīn rì cǐ mén zhōng
lines.lit: On this day last year, at this very gate,
lines.en: A year ago today, inside this gate,

lines.py: rén miàn táo huā xiāng yìng hóng
lines.lit: a face and peach blossoms reflected each other in pink.
lines.en: a face and peach blossoms glowed pink side by side.

lines.py: rén miàn bù zhī hé chù qù
lines.lit: The face — I do not know where it has gone;
lines.en: Where the face has gone, I cannot tell;

lines.py: táo huā yī jiù xiào chūn fēng
lines.lit: the peach blossoms, as before, smile in the spring wind.
lines.en: the peach blossoms still smile in the spring wind.

words.note: 现代汉语说“脸”；“人面桃花”是成语。
现代汉语常用，“依旧很美”。

words.en: to smile in the spring wind
words.note: 拟人写法，把桃花盛开说成在春风里笑。

imagery.name: 桃花
imagery.zh: 桃花年年照开，和姑娘的脸相映；人不见了，花还在，物是人非。
imagery.en: The blossoms return every year and once matched her face; now they bloom without her — the place is the same, the person gone.

imagery.name: 春风
imagery.zh: 春风里桃花“笑”着，越热闹越反衬诗人的失落。
imagery.en: The peach blossoms ‘smile’ in the spring wind, and their cheerfulness makes his loss sharper.
